name: Deal damage as a share of health
summary: A blast or hit removes a fixed share of each target's health instead of a set amount, so a big health pool is no defence and, in most versions, neither is armour (Dota 2's versions still let armour or magic resistance trim each hit): the heaviest tank loses the same share as a jeep. With a share of maximum health a few hits finish anything (three M.A.D. pulses wreck any vehicle or building not repaired in between); with a share of current health the hits shrink as the target weakens and never kill on their own, so teammates must finish. The M.A.D. pulse also spares soldiers and hurts its own side's machines as much as the enemy's. Because the biggest targets suffer most, it usually comes with a long, visible wind-up, a high price or a limit on what it can hit.
counterplay: Kill or stop the carrier before it goes off: the M.A.D. Tank's long, loud charge and the delayed crack of Earth Splitter both leave time to shoot it or step away.
Spread out and stay out of reach: every target in the area loses the same share, so a tight group of tanks loses the most.
Repair or heal between hits: a share of maximum health only kills if the hits land before repairs, and current-health versions can't kill alone.
Hunt the carrier with the kinds it ignores: soldiers walk through the M.A.D. pulse unhurt and can shoot the tank during its countdown.
Break line of sight where the effect needs it: terrain blocks Sombra's EMP.
Use targets that are immune to it, or make a target invulnerable for the moment; Red Alert's Iron Curtain also stalls the M.A.D. Tank's countdown.

other_examples.note: An ultimate that sends a long crack along the ground in front of the hero; after a short, visible delay it implodes, slowing every enemy on it for a few seconds and dealing damage equal to a share of its maximum health, half physical and half magical, which the target's armour and magic resistance then reduce. The delayed-line version: a telegraph that the enemy can step out of.

sources.title: Damage Types, Liquipedia Dota 2 Wiki
sources.note: Armour cuts physical damage and magic resistance cuts magical damage; Earth Splitter is listed among the abilities that deal physical damage.

other_examples.note: Marks out an area for several seconds; every second, each enemy inside takes a small set amount plus a share of its current health as magical damage, which magic resistance then reduces. The zone version, close to a hazard zone, that hurts big targets most.

sources.title: Enigma, Liquipedia Dota 2 Wiki
sources.note: The spell card gives the damage as magical spell damage, with the total stated before reductions.

sources.title: Damage Types, Liquipedia Dota 2 Wiki
sources.note: Magic resistance cuts magical damage, while armour only cuts physical damage.

other_examples.note: A recurring spell that cuts a target's health by a fixed fraction, often a half or a quarter. In most entries the fraction is of the health the target has left, so it can never kill; in a few it is of maximum health, which makes it lethal. Heavy enemies, and in some entries many other foes, are immune to it, the usual brake on fractional damage.

shooter_analogues.note: An ultimate that hits every enemy within a wide radius for a share of their current health, hacks them (their abilities go quiet for a few seconds) and destroys barriers; terrain blocks it. Patches have cut the share more than once and moved the ability's weight onto the disabling side: the current-health version as a team setup rather than a kill.

player_translation.summary: A signature ability that, after a long and loud wind-up, takes a fixed share of the health of every machine in a ring around the user. It guts clumps of heavy vehicles and fixed defences, rarely kills on its own, and in the M.A.D. version spares soldiers and hurts your own team's machines too.
as_user: You pick the moment: get into the thickest knot of enemy armour, press the key and hold through the wind-up; the payoff grows with how many machines are in the ring and how tough they are.
One hit seldom kills a healthy target, so plan the follow-up: your team's guns finish the weakened machines, or a second blast lands before they can repair.
Your teammates' machines inside the ring lose the same share, so you ping before you start.
Armour never protects the target, so your best targets are the most expensive, heaviest units on the field.
as_target: A ring on the ground and a rising siren show the reach and the time left: drive out, or kill the carrier before it fires.
Your armour won't help, so heavy tanks should leave first rather than trust their health.
If you are a soldier and the blast spares soldiers, you are the answer: walk in and shoot the carrier during its wind-up.
After a hit, back off and repair: the next blast finishes you only if you are still low.
teammates: Escorts that kill enemy infantry keep the carrier alive through the wind-up.
Setups (slows, pulls, stuns) hold enemy armour inside the ring, and finishers clean up the weakened machines afterwards.
On the receiving side, repairers and healers undo the damage between hits, and soldiers hunt the carrier.
Friendly vehicles clear the ring when the warning goes up, because the blast hurts them too.
controls: Q: start the blast, centred on you, on a spot within reach in the share-zone variant, or along a line in front of you in the delayed-line variant. The ring (or line) and the countdown appear at once on every screen.
One counted key. Pair it with a long cooldown, or with once per life in the blast-spends-user variant, where the blast also destroys the user.
feedback: A ground ring that fills as the charge builds, in team colour for allies and red for enemies, and a siren that every player on screen hears.
On the hit, every damaged target's health bar loses a visibly equal chunk, so players learn at a glance that armour didn't matter.
Units the blast ignores (soldiers in the M.A.D. version) show a small shield icon inside the ring.
Friendly machines inside the ring get a warning ping and an arrow out.
changes_from_rts: The M.A.D. pulse reaches well past the tank's own sight; here the ring must fit on screen so the people it hits can see it and react.
In Red Alert three pulses kill anything; against a unit a player paid for, one hit should take a moderate share, and blasts from several carriers should not stack freely.
The friendly damage is kept as the trade-off, but own-team players get the same ring and warning as the enemy.
The soldier immunity becomes an explicit, visible rule (shield icons in the ring) instead of a hidden property of the warhead.
Red Alert's 'unless repaired in between' becomes a designed window: teammates have time to repair a hit vehicle before a second blast.

team_play.notes: Heavy-armour teams must spread or bring the kinds it ignores; the user's team holds targets in the ring and finishes what it weakens; repairers on the receiving side decide whether a second hit kills.

notes: Damage as a share of maximum or current health is a short rule in the damage system, but it must bypass armour and resistances on purpose.
Needs a class or target-type filter (machines only, in the M.A.D. version) and a friendly-fire flag.
Objectives, bosses and buildings need a decision: immune, a reduced share, or full share.
UI: the reach ring, the countdown, equal-chunk health-bar feedback and immunity icons.
It hard-counters exactly the expensive heavy units that the price and tier system is meant to protect.
Several carriers together can delete anything if their shares stack; a shared cooldown or diminishing shares are needed.
Max-health shares stay strong all game, while flat damage falls behind as health grows, so tuning must look at the late tier.
Current-health versions can't kill alone but can make the next fight trivial for the user's team.
Players expect armour to matter; an equal chunk off every bar must be shown clearly or the result looks like a bug.
Players must know whether a hit took a share of maximum or of current health, since one can kill and the other can't.
Immunities (soldiers, bosses, objectives) have to be visible in the ring.

variants.name: Share of maximum health
variants.summary: Each hit takes the same share of maximum health, so a few hits finish anything that isn't repaired in between; the base form.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert M.A.D. Tank; Dota 2 Earth Splitter; Final Fantasy IX Demi

variants.name: Share of what is left
variants.summary: Each hit takes a share of the target's current health, so hits shrink as it weakens and can never kill on their own: a setup for teammates.
variants.seen_in: Overwatch 2 Sombra's EMP; most Final Fantasy Gravity spells

adds_weaknesses.why: Can never finish a target on its own, since each hit takes a share of what is left.

variants.name: Spares soldiers
variants.summary: The blast hurts only vehicles, aircraft and structures; soldiers walk through it unhurt and become its natural hunters.

counters.why: Every vehicle in the blast loses the same large share of its health whatever its armour, so a tank column is gutted at once.
Fixed defences can't leave the ring and lose a large share to every blast.

countered_by.why: Soldiers take no damage from the blast and can shoot the carrier through its whole wind-up.
Repairs between hits undo the damage before a follow-up can finish the target.
Fast units leave the blast area during the wind-up.

variants.name: Hits friend and foe
variants.summary: Every machine in the ring loses the same share, whoever owns it, so the user's team must clear out before it fires.

adds_weaknesses.why: One hit rarely kills: it needs a second hit or teammates to finish, and repairs in between undo it.
Its blast takes the same share from its own team's machines as from the enemy's.

variants.name: Blast that spends the user
variants.summary: The blast also destroys the user: it locks in place behind a long countdown, the player bails out as their infantry form when the countdown starts, and it can be used once per life. Only killing the user before the countdown ends stops it.

adds_weaknesses.why: One hit rarely kills: it needs a second hit or teammates to finish, and repairs in between undo it.
The blast spends the user, so it must arrive alive and gets one try per life.

countered_by.why: Repairs between hits undo the damage before a follow-up can finish the target.
Fast units leave the blast area during the wind-up.
Long-range guns destroy the locked-down user during its countdown, which stops the blast altogether.

variants.name: Delayed line
variants.summary: Instead of a ring around the user, a long line on the ground goes off after a short delay, slowing what it hits; victims who see the line can step off it.

variants.name: Draining zone
variants.summary: A field that, every second, takes a small share of the current health of each enemy inside, so big targets bleed fastest and leaving quickly is the answer.

adds_weaknesses.why: Hurts only what stays in the field, so targets that leave at once lose little.

countered_by.why: Fast units leave the field before it takes much.

adds_strengths.why: Each hit takes the same share of a target's health whatever its armour, so the toughest machines suffer most.

adds_weaknesses.why: One hit rarely kills: it needs a second hit or teammates to finish, and repairs in between undo it.

counters.why: Thick armour and big health pools give no protection against losing a share of health.

countered_by.why: Repairs between hits undo the damage before a follow-up can finish the target.
Fast units leave the blast area during the wind-up.

open_questions: Should the base default be a share of maximum health (lethal in a few hits) or of current health (a setup that can't kill)?
How should objectives, buildings and any boss-like targets take it: immune, a reduced share, or the full share?
Do blasts from several carriers stack freely, or share a cooldown or a diminishing share on the same target?
Is the soldier immunity part of the pattern, or one card's twist (the machines-only variant)?

shooter_fit.reason: One clear rule that strongly shapes counter-picks against heavy armour, and a wind-up ring gives good scramble moments, but it is mostly a damage formula: on its own it adds less interaction than its partner patterns, and the shares must stay moderate.
